title: CIZ1 regulates G1 length and the CDK threshold for initiation of DNA replication to prevent DNA replication stress

verified.what_i_actually_checked: Listed all 29 files in the Figshare record via its application programming interface (API): 27 time-lapse movies in AVI format (6-60 MB each), one 56 MB PowerPoint of supplementary figures, one 1.5 MB PDF of main figures; licence CC BY 4.0. Downloaded the smallest movie (6.5 MB) and read its header: Motion JPEG, 1900x1000 pixels, 184 frames, 10 frames per second - a lossy, montage-style display movie. Extracted the text layer of the figures PDF: it contains only axis labels and panel letters, no numeric tables. There is no comma-separated-value (CSV), spreadsheet or other tabular file anywhere in the record.
verified.what_came_from_paper_text_only: Sample sizes quoted in the text and figure legends (n = 3 biological replicates; 20-151 cells or nuclei per condition), the imaging set-up (DHB CDK-activity sensor plus histone H2B marker, Fucci(CA) cell-cycle reporter), and the DNA-fibre fork-rate measurements. Europe PMC's supplementary-files endpoint returned a non-archive 566-byte response, so the publisher-side supplement listing could not be retrieved; the 56 MB PowerPoint was over the 50 MB download cap and was recorded by name and size only.

a1_downloadable.note: Figshare record is public, CC BY 4.0, no login; I downloaded two files successfully.

a2_label_is_a_column.note: FAIL, verified in the files. There is no table of any kind - the entire deposit is 27 display movies plus two figure documents. Every quantity the paper reports (G1 phase length in hours, CDK sensor cytoplasmic-to-nuclear ratio at S-phase entry, replication fork rate) would have to be rebuilt from scratch by segmenting and tracking individual cells in lossy Motion-JPEG movies. That is constructing the label, not reading a column.

a3_inputs_present.note: FAIL. The movies are compressed, annotated presentation videos (Motion JPEG, multi-panel montages, channels split across separate files), not the raw per-channel intensity stacks. Quantitative features cannot be recovered reliably from them.

a4_units_stated.note: No data file exists to carry units; units appear only on figure axes in the PDF (hours, standardised fluorescence).

a5_enough_rows.note: FAIL. The unit of analysis is the tracked cell, and the paper reports n = 3 biological replicates with roughly 20-151 cells per condition across 27 movies - two to three orders of magnitude below the ~1,500-row bar. Counts taken from the paper text, since no file lists them.

a6_fits_laptop.note: Size is not the problem; the whole deposit is well under 1 GB.

a7_counts_match_paper.note: Cannot be checked - there are no counts in the deposit to compare against the paper's n values.

a8_label_provenance.note: Labels would come from our own segmentation and tracking of the authors' movies, i.e. a pipeline we build, applied to pixels we would also use as features. That is leakage-by-construction risk on top of having no measured label at all.

honest_claim_h3: No honest model claim is possible: the deposit contains no measured per-cell values, so any claim would be about a label we invented from the authors' display movies.

plain_idea.one_liner: Use early time-lapse images of a cell's CDK activity to predict when that cell starts copying its DNA.
plain_idea.train_on: The project considered would use per-cell time courses from live-cell movies of mouse fibroblasts carrying a CDK (cyclin-dependent kinase) activity sensor, in normal and CIZ1-knockout cells. The deposit supplies 27 movies; the paper quotes 20-151 cells per condition, so the number of usable cell tracks is in the low hundreds at best.
plain_idea.predict: Time from exit of quiescence to the start of DNA replication, and the CDK activity level at that moment. The true answer comes from fluorescence microscopy, but it exists only as points plotted in the paper's figures, not as any downloadable number.
plain_idea.why_worthwhile: Cell-cycle biologists studying the restriction point would like a quantitative rule linking early CDK dynamics to S-phase commitment; even a failed model would say whether early CDK trajectory carries that information. Neither is testable here because the measurements were not deposited.

ml_idea: Considered and rejected: predict S-phase entry time and the CDK activity threshold from the first hours of a single cell's CDK-sensor trace. Dead on arrival because the Figshare deposit holds only 27 compressed display movies and two figure files, with no per-cell measurement table and only a few hundred cells in total.

effort.compute_note: No modelling estimate made, because the feature/label table does not exist; building one would mean writing and validating a cell segmentation-and-tracking pipeline on lossy movies, which is a project in itself and would realistically want a graphics processing unit (GPU).
effort.cheapest_killing_check: List the Figshare files and look for any CSV or spreadsheet - 30 seconds, and it kills the project: 27 AVI movies, one PPTX, one PDF, zero tables.

verdict_reason: The deposited 'data' is 27 display movies plus figure files - no measurement table at all, so the prediction target would have to be constructed from pixels (A2, A3, A8 fail), and the paper's own n of roughly 20-151 cells per condition is far under the row threshold (A5).
